info.desc: The Immaculate Collection is the first greatest hits album by Madonna, released on November 9, 1990, by Sire Records. It contains new remixes of fifteen of her hit singles from 1983 to 1990, as well as two new songs. Its title is a pun on the Immaculate Conception, the conception of the Virgin Mary without the stain of original sin. An EP titled The Holiday Collection was released in Europe to accompany the compilation and the re-release of "Holiday", which included three hits not included on the main compilation. It is the first album ever to use the audio technology .

podcast.body: Issued in late 1990, this compilation became Madonna's first and best-selling greatest hits collection, achieving diamond sales. It controversially included "Into the Groove" (a non-charting US single) but omitted several of her 80s hits, including number ones like "Who's That Girl," "Angel," "Dress You Up," and "True Blue," demonstrating Madonna's confidence in shaping the narrative of her first decade. "In late 1990, Madonna issued her first and ultimately best selling greatest hits collection, the diamond selling the immaculate collection."
